title: Tau A152T risk variant drives distinct cell type transcriptional signatures in AD and PSP
title_zh: Tau A152T 风险变异在AD和PSP中驱动不同细胞转录特征
abstract: The A152T point mutation is a rare genetic variant in the tau gene (MAPT) that is linked to risk of Alzheimer's disease (AD) and frontotemporal dementia spectrum disorders, including progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP) and corticobasal degeneration (CBD). To uncover mechanisms through which the A152T variant contributes to risk of tauopathy, we performed single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) on postmortem brain tissue collected from A152T carriers and pathology-matched non-carriers with either AD or PSP, along with age-matched controls. These efforts revealed that despite similar cell type composition across groups, A152T carriers exhibited distinct cell type-specific transcriptional changes in both AD and PSP. Differential expression analysis identified excitatory neurons, oligodendrocytes, and astrocytes as the most affected cell populations in AD and PSP, and these same cell types showed the strongest A152T-specific changes. These findings identify transcriptional alterations that differentiate sporadic AD and sporadic PSP from AD-A152T and PSP-A152T, as well as shared molecular signatures unique to A152T carriers in both PSP and AD. Donor-level pseudo-bulk analyses showed broad directional support with the single-nucleus findings although the proportion of donor-supported genes varied across cell type and comparison. Importantly, merging sporadic and A152T cases into a single disease group was found to mask transcriptional differences in several cell types in both AD and PSP, indicating divergence in transcriptional signature and highlighting the importance of screening for genetic risk variants like A152T in snRNA-seq data from human cohorts.
abstract_zh: A152T点突变是tau基因(MAPT)中一种罕见的遗传变异，与阿尔茨海默病(AD)以及包括进行性上行性麻痹(PSP)和颞颞叶退行性变(CBD)在内的颞颞叶退行性谱系疾病的风险有关。为了阐明A152T变异如何导致tau病理的风险，我们在来自A152T载体和与其病理特征相匹配的非载体的AD或PSP后脑组织中进行了单核RNA测序(snRNA-seq)。尽管各组细胞类型组成相似，但A152T载体在AD和PSP中均表现出显著的细胞特异性转录变化。差异表达分析确定了兴奋性神经元、少突胶质细胞和星形胶质细胞为AD和PSP中最受影响的细胞群体，且这些细胞类型显示出最强的A152T特异性变化。这些发现鉴定出区分间发性AD和间发性PSP与AD-A152T和PSP-A152T的转录改变，以及在PSP和AD中均特异于A152T载体的共同分子特征。供体层面的伪体群分析显示单核测序结果有广泛的方向性支持，尽管支持基因的比例在细胞类型和比较 across 之间有所不同。重要的是，将间发性和A152T病例合并到单一疾病组中，在AD和PSP中均被发现掩盖了多个细胞类型的转录差异，表明转录特征存在分歧，并突出了在人类队列的snRNA-seq数据中筛查如A152T等遗传风险变异的重要性。
